messages:
ashley: Heads-up: prototyping an alternate "weight registry" handoff for warmup. Instead of manifest-first, registry returns streaming shard descriptors + causal provenance headers so loaders can choose eager/eager-lazy hybrid. Drafting interface; want opinions on atomicity and backpressure.

devon: Sounds promising. How does the registry handle partial uploads/rollbacks? main concern is atomic visibility for canary rollouts.

zara: If registry emits per-shard version + content-hash and a commit record, loaders can read shards idempotently. Rollbacks -> new commit that marks previous as deprecated. Loaders should bind to commit id.

ashley: Exactly — plan is: registry returns commit_id + list of shards with (shard_id, offset_range, size, checksum, store_url). Then a separate call to /commits/:id/state indicates COMMITTED vs PENDING vs DEPRECATED.

kevin: What about large checkpoints that may be uploaded concurrently? Do we serve while upload is still in-progress? That was causing OOMs previously.

priya: We should enforce a two-phase publish: staging upload -> verify checksums -> commit. For streaming reads during staging we can expose a 'read-only-incomplete' flag but disallow production routing.

infra-bot: deploy triggered: registry/commit-api v0.2 -> staging

devon: For warmup, loaders should be able to subscribe to commit stream and prefetch shards prioritized by activation map. Want a small backpressure signal from runtime: eg "prefetch_budget_remaining".

zara: Agree. Contract sketch:

HTTP GET /commits/:id
Response 200 {
  "commit_id": "c123",
  "state": "COMMITTED",
  "shards": [ { "shard_id":"s1", "range":"0-1048576", "size":"1MB", "checksum":"...", "url":"https://..." } ]
}

ashley: Also thinking about headers on the data stream: X-Shard-Sequence, X-Provenance, X-Epoch to help detect partial reads and allow resumable warmup.

kevin: How to handle compatibility with safetensors + gzipped chunks? URL may point to blob storage with content-encoding; loader must be able to handle content-negotiation.

priya: Suggest we include 'format' and 'encoding' fields in shard descriptor. e.g. "format": "safetensors", "encoding": "gzip".

devon: Operationally, what's the fallback if a shard read fails during warmup? Immediate retry? fallback to smaller model variant?

zara: Policy should be: retries up to N with exponential backoff, if still failing: mark shard as degraded and route requests to model-variant fallback. Emit telemetry: shard_warmup_failures, fallbacks_triggered.

ashley: OK next steps: I'll open an RFC PR with the commit API contract and loader changes. For now, any objections to two-phase commit + commit-state poll + commit-stream subscription?

kevin: no objections. add a 'quota' field for prefetching hints.

priya: I'll mock a loader shim implementing commit-bound loads and share perf numbers.

devon: +1 on commit-stream push model (webhook or SSE) to avoid polling.

ashley: nice. thanks. will follow up in RFC. :thumbsup:
